issues.description: The Rideable.messageOnRide method signature is inconsistent: the problem statement and the template Main expect a parameterless messageOnRide() returning a String (used as r.messageOnRide()), but the solution repository defines Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) and all implementations (Pig, Seal) use a String parameter. This parameter mismatch will prevent students from implementing and compiling code that follows the problem description or using the provided Main example, causing confusion about the intended interface contract.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable.messageOnRide signature consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution to match the problem/template by removing the equipment parameter: messageOnRide(): String and update Pig/Seal implementations accordingly, or (B) update the problem statement, UML, and template Main to require messageOnRide(String equipment) and adjust the example calls in Main to pass the equipment argument. Prefer option A to match the current problem description and template usage.

issues.description: The problem statement and template expect a zero-argument method messageOnRide() (interface Rideable and example calls in Main), but the solution changes the signature to messageOnRide(String equipment) in Rideable and its implementations (Pig, Seal). This signature/name mismatch prevents straightforward mapping from the exercise requirements and template usage to the solution: students following the problem/template would implement or call a no-arg messageOnRide(), while the solution defines and uses a different method signature and return format (adds an equipment suffix), creating confusion and compilation mismatch.
issues.suggestedFix: Restore the intended zero-argument signature: change Rideable.messageOnRide(String equipment) to messageOnRide() and update Pig and Seal implementations to match. Ensure the returned string follows the specification: "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]" (no equipment parameter) so template Main and problem statement align with the solution.
